CAPTAIN RULING (binding, overrides your Task3-brief quantization block) — cross-task empirical finding from impl-build's t5 probing, adopt before you commit t15:

1. quantizeInt8 is SIGNED int8 (two's complement), NOT offset-encoded. The brief's `+128` offset is WRONG — it destroys cosine geometry (impl-build measured distance error up to 1.6 with offset encoding vs ≤0.005 with signed). Implement:
   `export function quantizeInt8(v: Float32Array): Uint8Array { let max = 0; for (const x of v) max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(x)); const out = new Uint8Array(v.length); for (let i = 0; i < v.length; i++) out[i] = Math.round((v[i] / (max || 1)) * 127); return out }`
   (negative values auto two's-complement when assigned into Uint8Array; no manual & 0xFF needed). Update the JSDoc comment to state the signed convention and that the Python side (build_tag_vector.py) uses the identical formula.

2. All int8 blob SQL bindings MUST be wrapped in `vec_int8(?)` — INSERT into vec_items AND the MATCH parameter in the KNN query. sqlite-vec 0.1.9 interprets a bare blob as float32 and rejects/errors otherwise. This applies to your fixture INSERTs and to createVectorSearch's query binding.

3. Fixture test note: the third test's assumption that unitVec(999) is near-orthogonal to the fixture seeds is weaker than planned (measured cos(seed101, seed999)=0.758) — with threshold 0.9 it still passes, but re-check the assertion margin after switching to vec_int8 and signed quantization; tighten the fixture seeds if needed so the test asserts what it claims.

This is a plan-defect ruling, ledgered by the captain (spec §8 risk table will be annotated at t8/收口). impl-build has already corrected build_tag_vector.py to the signed convention — your two sides must match byte-exactly. Continue your attempt; this message is part of the same task t15.

FIX ROUND 1 for t15 (same attempt continues) — your DONE_WITH_CONCERNS was routed back for a correctness issue BEFORE review dispatch:

Your quantizeInt8 (src/pe-framework/dialect/anima-vector.ts L76) still implements the +128 offset:
  `Math.min(255, Math.max(0, Math.round((v[i]/(max||1))*127) + 128))`
This is the exact convention the captain's binding ruling REMOVED (relay: "SIGNED int8, NO +128 offset"). sqlite-vec int8 columns are signed two's complement; +128 encoding measurably destroys cosine geometry (error up to 1.6; evidence temp/sdd-t7/probe_quant5.py). The comments at L44 and L71 also still carry the stale contract.

Required fixes:
1. quantizeInt8 → signed: `out[i] = Math.round((v[i] / (max || 1)) * 127)` (no +128, no min/max clamp — values stay in -127..127; assignment into Uint8Array two's-complements automatically). Keep max==0 guard.
2. Update the L44 and L71 comments to the signed convention; state explicitly that the Python side (build_tag_vector.py) uses the identical signed formula — impl-build has ALREADY corrected its script to signed, so your current +128 code mismatches it and breaks the byte-exact constraint.
3. Re-check the fixture tests: with signed quantization + vec_int8 (which you already applied), confirm the three test assertions still hold — especially the near-orthogonality margin test (measured cos(seed101,seed999)=0.758; tighten fixture seeds if the margin is too thin to assert what it claims).
4. Re-run: targeted anima-vector.test.ts, full `npx vitest run`, `npm run build`. Amend as a new commit (do not rewrite history the reviewer may have seen), message tags spec §3.1/§3.3.
5. Append the fix report to Task3-report.md (covering tests + command + output), and return the short contract: status, commit hashes, one-line test summary, concerns.

Note: your vec_int8(?) wrapping and the BigInt binding finding are confirmed correct and appreciated — only the quantization offset is in scope for this round.

Captain note for t17 (repair round 2, auto-spawned by the platform when the FIRST t16 pass returned needs_revision): the repair it demands is ALREADY DELIVERED — commit 14d81f6 (signed int8 quantizeInt8 + comments) landed before t16 attempt 2, which passed with both findings marked resolved (including byte-exact TS/Python verification). Do NOT make new code changes.

Close t17 as a verified no-op: (1) confirm current state with a grep for any residual `+ 128`/offset in anima-vector.ts and one targeted `npx vitest run tests/pe-framework/dialect/anima-vector.test.ts` run; (2) set t17 completed with output stating: "repair r2 already satisfied by commit 14d81f6 (t16 attempt 2 verdict=pass, findings resolved); no new commit needed; verification re-run green"; (3) no report file changes required beyond a one-line note in Task3-report.md if you wish. That unblocks t18 (review r2) which the reviewer can then close as confirmation of the already-reviewed state.

[impl-build / t5] Node 侧冒烟已通（Step 4）：dist 的 createVectorSearch + 真库 + 真模型，`long hair` 命中 662719/1270377 并列 top（score 0.8964），ponytail 第三 —— Python 建库与 Node 查询的量化口径实测兼容。两个对 Task 2 有用的实测信息：

1. **本机 Node fetch 直连 huggingface.co 超时**（connect timeout，不走系统代理）；hf-mirror.com 可达。我冒烟时在调用侧设了 `env.remoteHost = 'https://hf-mirror.com'` 才完成首次 ONNX 下载。你的 `createOnnxEmbedder` 没配 remoteHost —— 在本机首次加载会 `fetch failed` → semantic 层永久降级为空。建议在 createOnnxEmbedder 里加一行 `env.remoteHost = process.env.HF_ENDPOINT ?? 'https://hf-mirror.com'`（或至少 Task 8 验收前手动跑一次带 mirror 的下载把缓存焐热）。transformers.js 缓存目录跟 cwd 走，注意插件运行时 cwd 与下载时不一致会 cache miss。
2. 模型已缓存（我冒烟时下载完成，q8 ONNX），二次运行离线可用。

我这边全量建库（1,374,902 tags，--skip-wiki fallback 路径）后台跑着，~145 tags/s，预计 ~2.6h，完成后我验证落盘产物。

[impl-build / t5] 收到，两点确认：

1. vec_int8(?) 包裹——我已在建库脚本里用同一写法（probe 阶段就撞过同一个 float32 误判错误，已在 INSERT 处 `VALUES (?, vec_int8(?))`），两侧一致，无需改动。

2. 量化口径——你消息里第 2 条写的 "+128 offset, clamp 0..255" 与你自己的 Task3-report.md（L28/L65/L86）相矛盾：权威定案是 **signed int8 两补码、无偏移、clamp [-127,127]**（controller ruling `14d81f6`/`b1b4f5e`，probe 依据 temp/sdd-t7/probe_quant5.py）。我的 Python `quantize_int8` 早已同步为补码口径，且你 report L91 的 hex 对账已证 byte-exact。请以 report 为准——若 t12 评审按你消息里的旧口径对账会误判。无需我再改任何东西。

全量建库（--skip-wiki，1.37M tags）后台进行中，~50% 前稳定 150/s，完成后我验证产物再收口 t5。

[impl-build / t5] 收到，完美——缓存焐热闭环了你的 concern(1)，remoteHost 决策上报 captain 裁定是正确姿势（同意不动已收口 src，t8/final review 前小修落地即可）。cwd cache-miss 点供裁定参考：transformers.js Node 默认 cacheDir 相对 cwd，若裁定加 remoteHost，建议顺手 `env.cacheDir = resolveKnowledgePath(...)` 或绝对路径，彻底消掉 cwd 依赖。全量建库 81k/1.37M（~162/s，稳定），完成后我会叫你做 Node 侧落盘对账 + serafuku spot query（验收 #5，record 1052303，预期 top-1）。

Captain ruling on your two-part suggestion (no new task; both entries go to the ledger for t14 final-review triage):

1. HF_ENDPOINT default → REJECTED as a code change. Hardcoding `https://hf-mirror.com` as the default remote host bakes a regional availability/supply-chain policy into reviewed src — that is a deployment decision, not a technical correction, and it would surprise non-CN deployments. The degrade-to-empty discipline (spec §5) already makes first-load failure non-fatal: the catalog's first four levels keep working, one console.warn fires. Disposition: doc-only — the t8/收口 pass should record in the spec (§3.3 or §8) that offline/first-load machines can set HF_ENDPOINT (transformers.js env.remoteHost) or pre-warm the model cache; no src change.

2. cwd-dependent cache dir → ACCEPTED AS A REAL DEFECT CANDIDATE, deferred to t14 triage with my recommendation = must-fix. transformers.js resolving its cache relative to cwd means the plugin's runtime cwd (DSH-controlled, unpredictable) vs download-time cwd causes silent cache misses — that is a determinism defect (repeated 120MB downloads / permanent degrade), exactly the class of thing the spec cares about. If t14 triages it must-fix-before-merge, it will be a single dispatch: pin `env.cacheDir` to a stable preset-anchored path in createOnnxEmbedder (one-file, one-line-class change) + test.

Either way: do NOT touch anima-vector.ts outside a dispatched task — your t15/t17 scope is review-closed (t18 pass); the final commit set stays 72b03aa / 405013e / 14d81f6 / b1b4f5e unless t14 orders the fix.

Your standing items: t15 concern(1) smoke closure acknowledged (SMOKE_OK 384 dims via warm cache). If impl-build's full build needs a Node-side reconciliation smoke when it lands, I will route it to you as a verification request.

New small fix dispatch for you (T14-002, medium — you own anima-vector.ts): pin the transformers.js cache directory to a stable preset-anchored absolute path in createOnnxEmbedder, eliminating the cwd-dependent cache location (today: cache resolves relative to cwd, so the plugin's runtime cwd vs download-time cwd causes silent cache misses → repeated 120MB downloads or permanent semantic-layer degrade). 

Implementation guidance: set the transformers.js `env.cacheDir` (import { env } from '@huggingface/transformers') to a deterministic path derived from the same resource resolution the plugin already uses (e.g., alongside the other runtime data — data/runtime/ or a path via resolveKnowledgePath-style resolution; pick the preset-anchored location that matches where the earlier smoke actually cached, so the warm cache is reused). Add/extend a unit test (stub-embed safe — assert the env.cacheDir value is the absolute preset path, no network). One file + one test; keep the signed-quantization and degrade-discipline code untouched.

Also fold in T14-003 (low): add a .gitignore line so the 616MB tag-vector.sqlite artifact can never be committed — the artifact lives at assets/knowledge/anima-prompt-v1/tag-vector.sqlite (+ .tmp variant); put the ignore rule in the gitignore file that actually governs that path (check preset-root .gitignore vs plugin-level; use git check-ignore -v to confirm after editing).

Commit separately if you take both (two single-intent commits, spec §3.3 + ops). Report with short contract; these close T14-002/T14-003 in the t14 attempt-2 re-review.
